# Fairwalter Public API

Reference documentation for the read-only Fairwalter public API, version `1.0.0`.

This repository is generated once a day from the live specification at [`https://my.fairwalter.ch/public-api/docs.json`](https://my.fairwalter.ch/public-api/docs.json). Everything below is produced from it — nothing here is written by hand, and the commit history is the changelog of the API.

- [`openapi.json`](openapi.json) — the OpenAPI 3 document, committed verbatim. Point a client generator at it.
- [`reference/`](reference/) — one page per resource: endpoints, parameters, field tables and an example response.
- [`llms.txt`](llms.txt) / [`llms-full.txt`](llms-full.txt) — the same reference in one file, for handing to an assistant.
- [Interactive API console](https://my.fairwalter.ch/public-api/docs) — execute a request against your own data (sign-in required).

---

Read-only public API v1.

The OpenAPI 3 document behind this page is served at `/public-api/docs.json` — point your code generator or HTTP client at it directly. It carries an absolute `servers[0].url`, so a generated client works without further configuration.

## Authentication

All `/public-api/v1` endpoints require a personal API token sent as a Bearer token in the `Authorization` header:

```
Authorization: Bearer fw_<your-token>
```

Tokens are issued per user and start with the `fw_` prefix. Contact your Fairwalter administrator to obtain a token.

### Using "Try it out"

Click the **Authorize** button at the top of this page, paste your `fw_...` token (Swagger UI adds the `Bearer ` prefix automatically), then use the "Try it out" buttons on individual endpoints.

## Resource model

Every resource is scoped to the customer the token belongs to, and further to the mandates the token may reach.

**Portfolio** — a one-to-many chain, each level carrying the FK of its parent:

```
Mandate → Property → Building → Object → Room
                                     ↘ Asset
```

- **Mandate** — the contract a property manager holds with an owner. Every other resource lives under exactly one mandate.
- **Property** — a land parcel under a mandate (`mandateId`).
- **Building** — sits on a property (`propertyId`).
- **Object** — a rental or ownership unit inside a building (`buildingId`).
- **Room** — a room inside an object (`objectId`).
- **Asset** — an appliance or installation, attached at whichever level it belongs to (`roomId`, `objectId`, `buildingId` or `propertyId`).

**Occupancy** — who uses an object, and under what agreement:

- **Contract** (`rent` only) — a tenancy on an object (`objectId`, `propertyId`, `mandateId`).
- **Owner** (`condo` only) — an ownership relation on an object. The condo counterpart of a contract, with its own vocabulary.
- **Person** — a natural person or company. Not mode-scoped: the same person can be a tenant here and an owner there. `roles` tells you which. Contracts and owners reference persons; use `filter[personId]` to go the other way.

**Finance** — the general ledger:

```
FiscalYear ──< OpeningBalance >── Account
     ╎                              ╎
     └──────< Booking >─────────────┘
```

- **FiscalYear** — either property-scoped (`type: accounting`, `propertyId` set) or a mandate-level rollup (`type: consolidation`, `mandateId` set). Exactly one of the two ids is non-null; the other is `null`.
- **Account** — one entry of the chart of accounts for the `{mode}` chart, with `number`, `label` and `category`.
- **OpeningBalance** — an account's balance carried into a fiscal year (`fiscalYearId`, `accountId`, `propertyId`).
- **Booking** — one journal entry (`debitAccountId`, `creditAccountId`, `propertyId`, optional `objectId`).
- **DebitorInvoice** — an outgoing invoice (`contractId`, `objectId`, `propertyId`, `mandateId`), the document behind most rent bookings.

**Operations and access:**

- **Damage** — a damage report (`objectId`, `buildingId`, `propertyId`, optional `serviceProviderId`).
- **ServiceProvider** — a trade contractor. Not mode-scoped.
- **User** — a property-management staff account, referenced by `managerId` on properties. Not mode-scoped.
- **File** — documents, listed under their owner (`/properties/{id}/files`, `/contracts/{id}/files`, …) and fetched by id via `getFile` / `downloadFile`.

Persons and mandates carry `name1` and `name2` (line 1 and line 2 of the name — company plus department, or last plus first name depending on `contactType`), not a single `name`. The one exception is the mandate sort key `sort=name`, which orders by `name1`.

Use `filter[*Id]` on list endpoints to traverse any of these edges. For example, `GET /public-api/v1/rent/objects?filter[propertyId]=42` returns every object under property 42.

## Modes

Most paths include a `{mode}` segment that selects the business domain:

- `rent` — rental-management data (`/public-api/v1/rent/...`).
- `condo` — condominium-ownership data (`/public-api/v1/condo/...`).

Mode constrains every related resource: a `rent` mandate only contains `rent` properties, buildings, and objects, and `{mode}/accounts` returns that mode's chart of accounts. `listMandates`, `listPersons`, `listServiceProviders` and `listUsers` carry no `{mode}` because they span both — mandates are the discriminator, so read `type` on a returned mandate to decide which mode to use for follow-up calls.

## Query parameters

- **Filter:** `filter[key]=value`. Allowed keys differ per endpoint and are listed on each operation.
- **Search:** `q=text` — case-insensitive partial match across the fields named in the `q` description.
- **Sort:** `sort=key` ascending, `sort=-key` descending.

Filters combine with `AND`; `q` narrows the same result set further.

### Bracket encoding

`filter[...]` contains characters that some clients and shells mangle. Either percent-encode the brackets, or disable globbing:

```bash
# Percent-encoded (works everywhere)
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer fw_..." \
  "https://app.fairwalter.ch/public-api/v1/rent/bookings?filter%5BfiscalYearId%5D=31&limit=500"

# Or -g / --globoff to keep the literal brackets
curl -g -H "Authorization: Bearer fw_..." \
  "https://app.fairwalter.ch/public-api/v1/rent/bookings?filter[fiscalYearId]=31&limit=500"
```

Most HTTP libraries encode query parameters for you; the problem is specific to shells and hand-built URLs.

## Response shapes

**List** endpoints wrap their rows in an envelope:

```json
{"data": [{"id": 1}, {"id": 2}], "meta": {"pagination": {"limit": 30, "offset": 0, "total": 2, "hasMore": false}}}
```

**Detail** endpoints return the bare object, with no `data` wrapper:

```json
{"id": 1}
```

This difference is deliberate — a single resource has no pagination to report. Detail responses also carry more fields than the list rows of the same resource.

**Amounts** are strings, never JSON numbers: a fixed two decimal places, `.` as the decimal separator, no thousands separator, no currency symbol (`"1700.00"`, `"-4420.00"`). Parse them as a decimal type with invariant culture — a de-CH locale parser reads `.` as a thousands separator and will silently turn `1700.00` into `170000`. Never parse them as floats.

All amounts are in **CHF**. Fairwalter is a single-currency product, so responses carry no `currency` field.

**Dates** are `YYYY-MM-DD` strings. Date-only fields have no time component or timezone.

## Pagination

List endpoints return at most `limit` items (default `30`) starting at `offset` (default `0`), plus a `meta.pagination` block with `limit`, `offset`, `total`, and `hasMore`. The maximum is `100` on most endpoints; export-oriented ones allow more (bookings: `500`). Each endpoint's `limit` parameter carries its own `maximum` in this spec, and a larger value is capped rather than rejected. To walk a full collection:

```text
offset = 0
loop:
  page = GET .../resources?limit=100&offset={offset}
  process(page.data)
  offset += page.data.length
  if not page.meta.pagination.hasMore: break
```

Prefer `hasMore` over `ceil(total/limit)` for the loop condition — `total` reflects the count at query time and may drift across pages if the underlying data changes. `limit=0` is accepted and silently normalized to 1; pass the endpoint's `maximum` for the largest page.

## Rate limits

Requests are limited to **600 per minute per token**, measured over a sliding window. Every response carries the current state:

| Header                  | Meaning                                             |
|-------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| `X-RateLimit-Limit`     | Requests allowed in the window.                     |
| `X-RateLimit-Remaining` | Requests left in the current window.                |
| `X-RateLimit-Reset`     | Unix timestamp (seconds) when the window refills.   |

Exceeding the limit returns `429` with error code `http` and a `Retry-After` header holding the number of seconds to wait. Honour it rather than retrying immediately; a bulk export that paginates at the endpoint's maximum page size stays far below the limit.

## Errors

Every error response uses the same JSON envelope:

```json
{
  "code": "badQuery",
  "message": "Unknown filter key: foo",
  "errors": [{"field": "filter.foo", "message": "Unknown filter key"}]
}
```

| Code              | HTTP   | Meaning                                                                |
|-------------------|--------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `badQuery`        | 400    | Malformed query — unknown filter/sort key, invalid pagination value.   |
| `unauthenticated` | 401    | Bearer token missing, malformed, or revoked.                           |
| `accessDenied`    | 403    | Token is valid but cannot reach the requested mandate or object scope. |
| `notFound`        | 404    | No resource with the requested id (or it sits outside the token scope).|
| `http`            | other 4xx | Other client-side error surfaced by the framework, including `429`. |
| `internal`        | 500    | Unhandled server error.                                                |

## Accounting

This section is the contract for anyone building a booking export or a financial statement.

### Sign convention

Every booking is a double entry: exactly one debit account, exactly one credit account, and a **positive** `amount`. The direction is carried by which account is which — there are no negative booking amounts.

Balances are **debit-positive**, and the same formula applies to every account regardless of category:

```
signed_movement(account) = Σ amounts where account is debitAccountId
                         − Σ amounts where account is creditAccountId

closing_balance(account) = opening_balance + signed_movement
```

That single rule is the whole convention. It follows that, in a normal year:

| Category      | Normal sign | Reads as              |
|---------------|-------------|-----------------------|
| `assets`      | ≥ 0         | Aktiven               |
| `liabilities` | ≤ 0         | Passiven (incl. equity) |
| `revenue`     | ≤ 0         | Ertrag                |
| `expenses`    | ≥ 0         | Aufwand               |

Contra accounts flip the sign of their category — a value correction inside `assets` is negative, a revenue reduction is positive. Do not "fix" a sign because it looks wrong for its category; the sign is the data.

`OpeningBalance.amount` is **already signed** with this convention (a credit-side opening balance is negative). Booking `amount` is not — it is always positive.

### Categories and account numbers

`Account.category` has four values. There is deliberately no `equity` category: Fairwalter's internal model has four, and equity accounts file under `liabilities`. The chart follows the Swiss KMU / Liegenschaften layout, so the account `number` gives you the finer structure:

| `category`    | Number range        | Swiss label                                             |
|---------------|---------------------|---------------------------------------------------------|
| `assets`      | 1xxx                | Aktiven                                                 |
| `liabilities` | 2xxx                | Passiven — including 28xx *Kapital der Eigentümer* and 29xx *Reserven und Jahresgewinn/-verlust* (equity) |
| `revenue`     | 3xxx                | Ertrag                                                  |
| `expenses`    | 4xxx–8xxx, and 9000 | Aufwand — 4xxx–6xxx operating, 8xxx extraordinary and non-operating, 9000 the closing account |

Two traps in that table:

- **Account 9000 (`Abschluss Erfolgsrechnung`) is categorised `expenses`.** Summing everything in `expenses` therefore double-counts the annual result of a closed year. Exclude it — see below.
- **The 8xxx block holds both extraordinary income and extraordinary expense** yet sits entirely in `expenses`. Its signed total is what matters, not its category.

Rely on `category` for the statement side and on `number` for subtotals and ordering. `/accounts` returns deactivated accounts too (`isActive: false`), because historic bookings still reference them.

### Unresolvable account ids

`{mode}/accounts` lists one chart — the `rent` chart or the `condo` chart. A booking can reference an account from the *other* chart (this occurs in practice on condo properties booking against rent-chart accounts). Such an id is absent from `{mode}/accounts`, and `{mode}/accounts/{id}` returns `404` for it.

This is why every booking carries `debitAccountNumber` and `creditAccountNumber` alongside the ids: **the number always resolves, even when the id does not.** A ledger export should read the numbers off the booking and never join at all.

If you do need the label or category of such an account, retry the id under the other mode (`/rent/accounts/{id}` when you are exporting `condo`, and vice versa) and fall back to rendering the number alone rather than aborting the export. Never assume every `debitAccountId` / `creditAccountId` on a booking page resolves within the chart you fetched.

### Closing entries

Closing a fiscal year posts one ordinary booking — nothing about it is a special record type:

- `type` is `closing_entry`, and it is the only booking touching account **9000**.
- It is dated the **last day of the fiscal year** and carries `reference` `A` + the 6-digit fiscal-year id (e.g. `A000031`).
- **Profit:** debit 9000 / credit **2990** (`Jahresgewinn oder -verlust`). **Loss:** the reverse, debit 2990 / credit 9000.

Consequences for a consumer:

- **Income statement (Erfolgsrechnung):** exclude the closing entry, or the result appears twice — once as the revenue/expense movement and once as the balance of 9000. Filter it out by `type != closing_entry`, or equivalently by skipping bookings that touch account 9000.
- **Balance sheet (Bilanz):** *include* it. Account 2990 is a `liabilities` account, and after closing it carries the annual result, which is what makes the closed year balance.

**Locked is not closed.** `FiscalYear.isLocked` means bookings can no longer be added or changed; it can be set and lifted on its own. Whether the year has been *closed* is a separate question — answered by whether a `closing_entry` booking exists for it. A year can be locked without a closing entry, and closed without being locked.

### VAT

Fairwalter does **not** track tax codes or tax rates on bookings. There is no VAT field to export, and no way to split an amount into net and tax. Amounts are exactly as booked.

### The `reference` field

`reference` groups the bookings that came out of one source document. Every booking generated from the same invoice carries that invoice's reference, so grouping a page of bookings by `reference` reconstructs the documents behind them. The first character indicates the document type:

| Prefix | Source document                |
|--------|--------------------------------|
| `D`    | Debitor (outgoing) invoice     |
| `K`    | Creditor (incoming) invoice    |
| `G`    | Creditor reimbursement         |
| `N`    | Ancillary-expense settlement   |
| `L`    | Vacancy                        |
| `M`    | Manual booking                 |
| `A`    | Closing entry                  |

Two limits, both load-bearing:

- **It is not a voucher id.** The sequence is per customer, and a combined invoice re-stamps its sub-invoices with the parent's reference — so one reference can legitimately span several invoices. Use it for grouping, never as a primary key.
- **Do not derive the booking type from the prefix.** Historic and migrated data mixes them (creditor bookings carrying `M`, ancillary bookings carrying `D`). The `type` field is authoritative.

On `manual` bookings `reference` is whatever the user typed, so it need not follow any of this.

### Building a Bilanz and an Erfolgsrechnung

1. **Pick the fiscal year.** `GET /{mode}/fiscal-years` → note the `id`, `starts`, `ends`. `type: accounting` years are per property; `type: consolidation` years roll up a mandate.
2. **Fetch the chart.** `GET /{mode}/accounts?limit=100` (paginate) → map `id` → `{number, label, category, group}`. `category` decides the statement side, `group` gives you the subtotal headings, `number` the ordering.
3. **Fetch opening balances.** `GET /{mode}/opening-balances?filter[fiscalYearId]={id}&limit=100` (paginate) → map `accountId` → signed `amount`. Accounts with no row open at `0`.
4. **Fetch the journal.** `GET /{mode}/bookings?filter[fiscalYearId]={id}&limit=500` (paginate). The fiscal-year filter resolves to that year's property and date range for you.
5. **Accumulate.** For each booking add `amount` to its `debitAccountId` and subtract it from its `creditAccountId`. That yields `signed_movement` per account.
6. **Erfolgsrechnung** — movement only, opening balances are irrelevant. Take accounts with `category` `revenue` or `expenses`, **skip the closing entry**, and report `-signed_movement` for revenue (so income reads positive) and `signed_movement` for expenses. Result = revenue − expenses.
7. **Bilanz** — `opening_balance + signed_movement` for accounts with `category` `assets` or `liabilities`, **including** the closing entry.

**Reconciliation checks** — run these before trusting the output:

- Every booking page: `Σ debits = Σ credits` by construction, so the signed movement across *all* accounts must be `0`.
- Closed year: `Σ assets = −Σ liabilities` (Aktiven = Passiven), and `Σ revenue + Σ expenses + balance(9000) = 0`.
- Open year (no closing entry yet): `Σ assets + Σ liabilities = −(Σ revenue + Σ expenses)` — the difference between Aktiven and Passiven *is* the year's result.

### Worked example

One property, fiscal year `31` (2025). Opening balances:

| Account | Category    | `amount`     |
|---------|-------------|--------------|
| 1020 Bank | assets    | `"15230.45"` |
| 2000 Kreditoren | liabilities | `"-4100.00"` |
| 2800 Kapital der Eigentümer | liabilities | `"-11130.45"` |

Opening sums to `0`, as it must. Three bookings during the year:

| Date | Debit | Credit | `amount` | `type` |
|------|-------|--------|----------|--------|
| 2025-03-01 | 1100 Forderungen Mieter | 3000 Mietzins | `"1700.00"` | `debitor_invoice` |
| 2025-03-05 | 1020 Bank | 1100 Forderungen Mieter | `"1700.00"` | `debitor_invoice` |
| 2025-04-10 | 4131 Betriebskosten | 2000 Kreditoren | `"320.00"` | `creditor_invoice` |

Signed movements: `1020 +1700.00`, `1100 0.00`, `3000 −1700.00`, `4131 +320.00`, `2000 −320.00`.

**Erfolgsrechnung:** Ertrag `−(−1700.00) = 1700.00`, Aufwand `320.00`, result **`1380.00`** profit.

Closing therefore posts `debit 9000 / credit 2990`, `"1380.00"`, dated `2025-12-31`, `type: closing_entry`, `reference: "A000031"`.

**Bilanz after closing:**

| Account | Opening | Movement | Closing |
|---------|---------|----------|---------|
| 1020 Bank | `15230.45` | `+1700.00` | `16930.45` |
| 1100 Forderungen | `0.00` | `0.00` | `0.00` |
| 2000 Kreditoren | `-4100.00` | `-320.00` | `-4420.00` |
| 2800 Kapital | `-11130.45` | `0.00` | `-11130.45` |
| 2990 Jahresgewinn | `0.00` | `-1380.00` | `-1380.00` |

Aktiven `16930.45`, Passiven `−16930.45` — balanced. Before the closing entry existed, Aktiven `16930.45` minus Passiven `15550.45` would have left exactly the `1380.00` result.

## Common workflows

**Find every object in a property.** Call `GET /public-api/v1/{mode}/objects?filter[propertyId]={id}` and walk pages until `meta.pagination.hasMore` is `false`.

**Find buildings by address.** Call `GET /public-api/v1/{mode}/buildings?q=Bahnhofstrasse` and inspect `street` / `houseNumber` on the returned items.

**Fetch every resource of a type.** Start at `offset=0` with the endpoint's maximum `limit`, increment `offset` by `data.length` each round, stop when `meta.pagination.hasMore` is `false`.

**Export a year's journal for an accounting package.** Resolve the fiscal year, then page `/{mode}/bookings?filter[fiscalYearId]={id}&limit=500`. Each row already carries `debitAccountNumber` and `creditAccountNumber`, so no account lookup is needed at all — pull `/{mode}/accounts` only if your target system also wants account labels. Group by `reference` if it wants one voucher per document.

## Read-only safety

The API exposes `GET` operations only. No write, update, or delete endpoints exist — calling this API never modifies Fairwalter data.

# Account

| Method | Path | Operation | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/public-api/v1/{mode}/accounts` | `listAccounts` | List the chart of accounts |
| GET | `/public-api/v1/{mode}/accounts/{id}` | `getAccount` | Get a single account |

## GET /public-api/v1/{mode}/accounts

**List the chart of accounts** — `listAccounts`

Returns the customer's own chart of accounts for the selected `{mode}` chart
(rent/condo). The chart is customer-level, so every token of the customer sees the
same accounts.

Narrow with `filter[category]`. Use `q` to search by `label` (substring) or
`number` (prefix).

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | query | integer |  | Maximum number of items to return. limit=0 is accepted and silently treated as 1. Values above the maximum are capped to it. Default `30`. Maximum `100`. |
| `offset` | query | integer |  | Number of items to skip. Use with limit for pagination. Default `0`. |
| `q` | query | string |  | Free-text search across: number, label. Case-insensitive partial match; every word must match one of these fields (so "Peter Berger" matches first and last name in separate fields). Combine with filter[...] keys to narrow further. |
| `filter[category]` | query | string: `assets` \| `liabilities` \| `revenue` \| `expenses` |  | Restricts results to records matching the given category. |
| `sort` | query | string: `number` \| `-number` \| `id` \| `-id` |  | Sort field. Prefix with `-` for descending order (e.g. `-number`). Allowed: number, id. |
| `mode` | path | string: `rent` \| `condo` | yes | Business domain for the request. Use `rent` for rental-management data, `condo` for condominium-ownership data. The selected mode constrains every related resource. |

**List capabilities**

- **Searchable (`q`):** number, label
- **Filterable:** `filter[category]` (`assets`, `liabilities`, `revenue`, `expenses`)
- **Sortable:** `number`, `id` (prefix `-` for descending)
- **Page size:** default `30`, maximum `100`

**Response** — `200` returns a list envelope around [AccountApiResponse](#accountapiresponse).

| Status | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | OK |
| `400` | Invalid query parameters |
| `401` | Missing or invalid token |
| `403` | Token cannot access this resource |
| `429` | Rate limit exceeded |

**Example response**

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": 1,
      "number": 1020,
      "label": "Bank",
      "category": "assets",
      "group": {
        "id": 17,
        "label": "Kapital der Eigentümer"
      }
    }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "pagination": {
      "limit": 30,
      "offset": 0,
      "total": 1,
      "hasMore": false
    }
  }
}
```

## GET /public-api/v1/{mode}/accounts/{id}

**Get a single account** — `getAccount`

Returns one account of the customer's own `{mode}` chart by id. Returns 404 when the
account does not exist, is not on the `{mode}` chart, or belongs to another customer.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | integer | yes |  |
| `mode` | path | string: `rent` \| `condo` | yes | Business domain for the request. Use `rent` for rental-management data, `condo` for condominium-ownership data. The selected mode constrains every related resource. |

**Response** — `200` returns [AccountApiResponse](#accountapiresponse).

| Status | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | OK |
| `401` | Missing or invalid token |
| `403` | Token cannot access this resource |
| `404` | Account not found |
| `429` | Rate limit exceeded |

**Example response**

```json
{
  "id": 1,
  "number": 1020,
  "label": "Bank",
  "category": "assets",
  "group": {
    "id": 17,
    "label": "Kapital der Eigentümer"
  }
}
```

## Schemas

### AccountApiResponse

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | integer | yes |  |
| `number` | integer | yes | Account number, e.g. 1000. |
| `label` | string | yes |  |
| `category` | [AccountCategory](#accountcategory) | yes |  |
| `group` | [AccountGroupResponse](#accountgroupresponse) | yes |  |

### AccountCategory

String enum, 4 values.

`assets`, `liabilities`, `revenue`, `expenses`

### AccountGroupResponse

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | integer | yes | Stable id of the group. Groups are part of the chart of accounts, not customer data. |
| `label` | string | yes | German group heading as it appears on a financial statement. |

### PaginationMeta

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | integer | yes |  |
| `offset` | integer | yes |  |
| `total` | integer | yes |  |
| `hasMore` | boolean | yes |  |

# Asset

| Method | Path | Operation | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/public-api/v1/{mode}/assets` | `listAssets` | List assets |
| GET | `/public-api/v1/{mode}/assets/{id}` | `getAsset` | Get asset details |

## GET /public-api/v1/{mode}/assets

**List assets** — `listAssets`

Returns the assets (equipment/installations) of rental objects reachable for the
selected `{mode}`. Each asset carries `roomId` and `objectId` FKs that resolve via
`getRoom` and `getObject`.

Scope with `filter[roomId]`, `filter[objectId]`, `filter[buildingId]`, or
`filter[propertyId]`; use `q` to search across name, manufacturer, model and serial number.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | query | integer |  | Maximum number of items to return. limit=0 is accepted and silently treated as 1. Values above the maximum are capped to it. Default `30`. Maximum `100`. |
| `offset` | query | integer |  | Number of items to skip. Use with limit for pagination. Default `0`. |
| `q` | query | string |  | Free-text search across: name, manufacturer, model, serialNo. Case-insensitive partial match; every word must match one of these fields (so "Peter Berger" matches first and last name in separate fields). Combine with filter[...] keys to narrow further. |
| `filter[roomId]` | query | integer |  | Restricts results to records belonging to the given room id. |
| `filter[objectId]` | query | integer |  | Restricts results to records belonging to the given object id. |
| `filter[buildingId]` | query | integer |  | Restricts results to records belonging to the given building id. |
| `filter[propertyId]` | query | integer |  | Restricts results to records belonging to the given property id. |
| `sort` | query | string: `id` \| `-id` \| `name` \| `-name` \| `nextServiceDate` \| `-nextServiceDate` |  | Sort field. Prefix with `-` for descending order (e.g. `-id`). Allowed: id, name, nextServiceDate. |
| `mode` | path | string: `rent` \| `condo` | yes | Business domain for the request. Use `rent` for rental-management data, `condo` for condominium-ownership data. The selected mode constrains every related resource. |

**List capabilities**

- **Searchable (`q`):** name, manufacturer, model, serialNo
- **Filterable:** `filter[roomId]`, `filter[objectId]`, `filter[buildingId]`, `filter[propertyId]`
- **Sortable:** `id`, `name`, `nextServiceDate` (prefix `-` for descending)
- **Page size:** default `30`, maximum `100`

## GET /public-api/v1/{mode}/assets/{id}

**Get asset details** — `getAsset`

Returns a single asset by id, including its template `category`, identification
(manufacturer, model, serial number), and service/guarantee dates.

Use `listAssets` for discovery when the id is unknown. The `roomId` / `objectId` FKs
link back to `getRoom` / `getObject`.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |

# Booking

| Method | Path | Operation | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/public-api/v1/{mode}/bookings` | `listBookings` | List bookings (journal) |
| GET | `/public-api/v1/{mode}/bookings/{id}` | `getBooking` | Get a booking |

## GET /public-api/v1/{mode}/bookings

**List bookings (journal)** — `listBookings`

Returns the journal entries reachable for the selected `{mode}`. Every booking is a
double entry with exactly one debit and one credit account and a positive amount.

The primary export flow is `filter[fiscalYearId]` (resolved to the year's
property/mandate and date range). Narrow further with `filter[dateFrom]` /
`filter[dateTo]` (inclusive range), `filter[accountId]` (debit or credit side),
`filter[propertyId]`, or `filter[type]`. Use `q` to search by label or reference.
This endpoint allows a larger page size (up to 500) for full-year exports.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | query | integer |  | Maximum number of items to return. limit=0 is accepted and silently treated as 1. Values above the maximum are capped to it. Default `30`. Maximum `500`. |
| `offset` | query | integer |  | Number of items to skip. Use with limit for pagination. Default `0`. |
| `q` | query | string |  | Free-text search across: label, reference. Case-insensitive partial match; every word must match one of these fields (so "Peter Berger" matches first and last name in separate fields). Combine with filter[...] keys to narrow further. |
| `filter[fiscalYearId]` | query | integer |  | Restricts results to records belonging to the given fiscalYear id. |
| `filter[dateFrom]` | query | string (date) |  | Lower (inclusive) bound: only records whose date is on or after this value. |
| `filter[dateTo]` | query | string (date) |  | Upper (inclusive) bound: only records whose date is on or before this value. |
| `filter[accountId]` | query | integer |  | Restricts results to records belonging to the given account id. |
| `filter[propertyId]` | query | integer |  | Restricts results to records belonging to the given property id. |
| `filter[type]` | query | string: `debitor_invoice` \| `creditor_invoice` \| `ancillary_expense` \| `vacancy` \| `reimbursement_invoice` \| `manual` \| `closing_entry` |  | Restricts results to records matching the given type. |
| `sort` | query | string: `date` \| `-date` \| `id` \| `-id` |  | Sort field. Prefix with `-` for descending order (e.g. `-date`). Allowed: date, id. |
| `mode` | path | string: `rent` \| `condo` | yes | Business domain for the request. Use `rent` for rental-management data, `condo` for condominium-ownership data. The selected mode constrains every related resource. |

**List capabilities**

- **Searchable (`q`):** label, reference
- **Filterable:** `filter[fiscalYearId]`, `filter[dateFrom]`, `filter[dateTo]`, `filter[accountId]`, `filter[propertyId]`, `filter[type]` (`debitor_invoice`, `creditor_invoice`, `ancillary_expense`, `vacancy`, `reimbursement_invoice`, `manual`, `closing_entry`)
- **Sortable:** `date`, `id` (prefix `-` for descending)
- **Page size:** default `30`, maximum `500`

**Response** — `200` returns a list envelope around [BookingApiResponse](#bookingapiresponse).

| Status | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | OK |
| `400` | Invalid query parameters |
| `401` | Missing or invalid token |
| `403` | Token cannot access this resource |
| `429` | Rate limit exceeded |

**Example response**

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": 1,
      "debitAccountId": 45,
      "debitAccountNumber": 1100,
      "creditAccountId": 12,
      "creditAccountNumber": 3000,
      "propertyId": 7,
      "objectId": 789,
      "date": "2025-03-01",
      "label": "Mietzins März 2025, Bahnhofstrasse 1, 2.OG",
      "reference": "RE-2025-0341",
      "type": "debitor_invoice",
      "amount": "1700.00"
    }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "pagination": {
      "limit": 30,
      "offset": 0,
      "total": 1,
      "hasMore": false
    }
  }
}
```

## GET /public-api/v1/{mode}/bookings/{id}

**Get a booking** — `getBooking`

Returns a single journal entry by id. Returns 404 when it does not exist, is outside
the token's scope, or does not belong to the selected `{mode}`.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | integer | yes |  |
| `mode` | path | string: `rent` \| `condo` | yes | Business domain for the request. Use `rent` for rental-management data, `condo` for condominium-ownership data. The selected mode constrains every related resource. |

**Response** — `200` returns [BookingApiResponse](#bookingapiresponse).

| Status | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | OK |
| `401` | Missing or invalid token |
| `403` | Token cannot access this resource |
| `404` | Booking not found |
| `429` | Rate limit exceeded |

**Example response**

```json
{
  "id": 1,
  "debitAccountId": 45,
  "debitAccountNumber": 1100,
  "creditAccountId": 12,
  "creditAccountNumber": 3000,
  "propertyId": 7,
  "objectId": 789,
  "date": "2025-03-01",
  "label": "Mietzins März 2025, Bahnhofstrasse 1, 2.OG",
```

## Schemas

### BookingApiResponse

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | integer | yes |  |
| `debitAccountId` | integer | yes | FK to the debit account (Soll). Resolve via `getAccount`. |
| `debitAccountNumber` | integer | yes | Account number of the debit account, embedded so a ledger export needs no join. Resolves even when the account sits on the other `{mode}` chart and `getAccount` would 404. |
| `creditAccountId` | integer | yes | FK to the credit account (Haben). Resolve via `getAccount`. |
| `creditAccountNumber` | integer | yes | Account number of the credit account. See `debitAccountNumber`. |
| `propertyId` | integer | yes | FK to the property. Resolve via `getProperty`. |
| `objectId` | integer · nullable |  | FK to the object when the booking is attributable to a single object; otherwise null. |
| `date` | string (date) | yes |  |
| `label` | string | yes | Booking text. |
| `reference` | string · nullable |  | Free-text reference (e.g. invoice number); null when none. |
| `type` | [BookingType](#bookingtype) | yes |  |
| `amount` | string | yes | Booking amount as a fixed two-decimal string — always positive (direction is given by the debit/credit accounts). |

### BookingType

String enum, 7 values.

`debitor_invoice`, `creditor_invoice`, `ancillary_expense`, `vacancy`, `reimbursement_invoice`, `manual`, `closing_entry`

# Building

| Method | Path | Operation | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/public-api/v1/{mode}/buildings` | `listBuildings` | List buildings |

| GET | `/public-api/v1/{mode}/buildings/{id}` | `getBuilding` | Get building details |

## GET /public-api/v1/{mode}/buildings

**List buildings** — `listBuildings`

Returns buildings under reachable properties for the selected `{mode}`.

Buildings sit between properties and objects in the resource hierarchy (`Mandate → Property → Building → Object`). Each building carries a `propertyId` FK that resolves via `getProperty`.

Scope with `filter[propertyId]` (single property) or `filter[mandateId]` (every building under one mandate). Use `q` for free-text search across name, street, ZIP and city.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | query | integer |  | Maximum number of items to return. limit=0 is accepted and silently treated as 1. Values above the maximum are capped to it. Default `30`. Maximum `100`. |
| `offset` | query | integer |  | Number of items to skip. Use with limit for pagination. Default `0`. |
| `q` | query | string |  | Free-text search across: name, street, postcode, city. Case-insensitive partial match; every word must match one of these fields (so "Peter Berger" matches first and last name in separate fields). Combine with filter[...] keys to narrow further. |
| `filter[propertyId]` | query | integer |  | Restricts results to records belonging to the given property id. |
| `filter[mandateId]` | query | integer |  | Restricts results to records belonging to the given mandate id. |
| `sort` | query | string: `id` \| `-id` \| `name` \| `-name` \| `street` \| `-street` |  | Sort field. Prefix with `-` for descending order (e.g. `-id`). Allowed: id, name, street. |
| `mode` | path | string: `rent` \| `condo` | yes | Business domain for the request. Use `rent` for rental-management data, `condo` for condominium-ownership data. The selected mode constrains every related resource. |

**List capabilities**

- **Searchable (`q`):** name, street, postcode, city
- **Filterable:** `filter[propertyId]`, `filter[mandateId]`
- **Sortable:** `id`, `name`, `street` (prefix `-` for descending)
- **Page size:** default `30`, maximum `100`

**Response** — `200` returns a list envelope around [BuildingApiResponse](#buildingapiresponse).

| Status | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | OK |
| `400` | Invalid query parameters |
| `401` | Missing or invalid token |
| `403` | Token cannot access this resource |
| `429` | Rate limit exceeded |

**Example response**

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": 1,
      "propertyId": 1,
      "name": "string",
      "street": "string",
      "houseNumber": "string",
      "egid": "123456789",
      "buildYear": 1998,
      "lastRenovation": 2018,
      "startOfRenting": "2021-01-01"
    }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "pagination": {
      "limit": 30,
      "offset": 0,
      "total": 1,
      "hasMore": false
    }
  }
}
```

## GET /public-api/v1/{mode}/buildings/{id}

**Get building details** — `getBuilding`

Returns a single building by id, including its address, EGID, build year, and `startOfRenting` date.

Use `listBuildings` for discovery when the id is unknown. The `propertyId` FK links back to `getProperty`; `getObject` / `listObjects` traverse down to objects inside this building.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | integer | yes |  |
| `mode` | path | string: `rent` \| `condo` | yes | Business domain for the request. Use `rent` for rental-management data, `condo` for condominium-ownership data. The selected mode constrains every related resource. |

**Response** — `200` returns [BuildingApiResponse](#buildingapiresponse).

| Status | Description |
| --- | --- |

| `429` | Rate limit exceeded |

```json
{
  "id": 1,
  "propertyId": 1,
  "name": "string",
  "street": "string",
```

# Contract

| Method | Path | Operation | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/public-api/v1/rent/contracts` | `listContracts` | List rent contracts |
| GET | `/public-api/v1/rent/contracts/{id}/files` | `listContractFiles` | List files of a contract |
| GET | `/public-api/v1/rent/contracts/{id}` | `getContract` | Get rent contract details |

## GET /public-api/v1/rent/contracts

**List rent contracts** — `listContracts`

Returns rent contracts (tenancies) reachable by the token, including vacancy
periods (`isVacancy: true`). Each row carries the derived `status`, the linked
`persons`, and the `currentRent` effective today; the full rent version history
is on the detail endpoint.

Narrow with `filter[status]`, `filter[isVacancy]`, `filter[mainContractId]`,
`filter[personId]`, `filter[objectId]`, `filter[propertyId]` or
`filter[mandateId]`. Use `q` to search by linked person name.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | query | integer |  | Maximum number of items to return. limit=0 is accepted and silently treated as 1. Values above the maximum are capped to it. Default `30`. Maximum `100`. |
| `offset` | query | integer |  | Number of items to skip. Use with limit for pagination. Default `0`. |
| `q` | query | string |  | Free-text search across: name1, name2. Case-insensitive partial match; every word must match one of these fields (so "Peter Berger" matches first and last name in separate fields). Combine with filter[...] keys to narrow further. |
| `filter[status]` | query | string: `upcoming` \| `active` \| `noticed` \| `terminated` |  | Restricts results to records matching the given status. |
| `filter[isVacancy]` | query | string: `true` \| `false` |  | Restricts results to records matching the given isVacancy. |
| `filter[mainContractId]` | query | integer |  | Restricts results to records belonging to the given mainContract id. |
| `filter[personId]` | query | integer |  | Restricts results to records belonging to the given person id. |
| `filter[objectId]` | query | integer |  | Restricts results to records belonging to the given object id. |
| `filter[propertyId]` | query | integer |  | Restricts results to records belonging to the given property id. |
| `filter[mandateId]` | query | integer |  | Restricts results to records belonging to the given mandate id. |
| `sort` | query | string: `id` \| `-id` \| `starts` \| `-starts` |  | Sort field. Prefix with `-` for descending order (e.g. `-id`). Allowed: id, starts. |

**List capabilities**

- **Searchable (`q`):** name1, name2
- **Filterable:** `filter[status]` (`upcoming`, `active`, `noticed`, `terminated`), `filter[isVacancy]` (`true`, `false`), `filter[mainContractId]`, `filter[personId]`, `filter[objectId]`, `filter[propertyId]`, `filter[mandateId]`
- **Sortable:** `id`, `starts` (prefix `-` for descending)
- **Page size:** default `30`, maximum `100`

**Response** — `200` returns a list envelope around [ContractApiResponse](#contractapiresponse).

| Status | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | OK |
| `400` | Invalid query parameters |
| `401` | Missing or invalid token |

## GET /public-api/v1/rent/contracts/{id}/files

**List files of a contract** — `listContractFiles`

Returns the files attached to a rent contract. Visible exactly when the contract is visible via `getContract`.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | query | integer |  | Maximum number of items to return. limit=0 is accepted and silently treated as 1. Values above the maximum are capped to it. Default `30`. Maximum `100`. |
| `offset` | query | integer |  | Number of items to skip. Use with limit for pagination. Default `0`. |
| `q` | query | string |  | Free-text search across: name. Case-insensitive partial match; every word must match one of these fields (so "Peter Berger" matches first and last name in separate fields). Combine with filter[...] keys to narrow further. |
| `filter[category]` | query | string enum (18 values) |  | Restricts results to records matching the given category. One of: `finance`, `contracts`, `correspondence`, `protocol`, `personal_information`, `state_documents`, `repairs_and_damage`, `pictures`, `various`, `rules_and_regulations`, `locking_schedule`, `plan`, `service_contracts`, `insurance`, `offer`, `condominium_protocol`, `condominium_meeting`, `profile_image`. |
| `sort` | query | string: `id` \| `-id` \| `name` \| `-name` \| `uploadedAt` \| `-uploadedAt` \| `fileSize` \| `-fileSize` |  | Sort field. Prefix with `-` for descending order (e.g. `-id`). Allowed: id, name, uploadedAt, fileSize. |
| `id` | path | integer | yes |  |

**List capabilities**

- **Searchable (`q`):** name
- **Filterable:** `filter[category]` (`finance`, `contracts`, `correspondence`, `protocol`, `personal_information`, `state_documents`, `repairs_and_damage`, `pictures`, `various`, `rules_and_regulations`, `locking_schedule`, `plan`, `service_contracts`, `insurance`, `offer`, `condominium_protocol`, `condominium_meeting`, `profile_image`)
- **Sortable:** `id`, `name`, `uploadedAt`, `fileSize` (prefix `-` for descending)
- **Page size:** default `30`, maximum `100`

**Response** — `200` returns a list envelope around [FileApiResponse](#fileapiresponse).

| Status | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | OK |
| `400` | Invalid query parameters |
| `401` | Missing or invalid token |
| `403` | Token cannot access this resource |
| `404` | Parent resource not found |
| `429` | Rate limit exceeded |

**Example response**

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": 4711,
      "name": "Hausordnung.pdf",
      "category": "finance",
      "mimeType": "application/pdf",
      "fileSize": 184320,
      "uploadedAt": "2026-03-14T09:12:00+01:00"
    }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "pagination": {
      "limit": 30,
      "offset": 0,
      "total": 1,
      "hasMore": false
    }
  }
}
```

## GET /public-api/v1/rent/contracts/{id}

**Get rent contract details** — `getContract`

Returns a single rent contract (or vacancy entry) by id, including the linked
`persons`, deposit, notice details, the `currentRent`, and the full `rents`
version history. Returns 404 when the contract does not exist, is not a rent
contract, or is outside the token's scope.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | integer | yes |  |

**Response** — `200` returns [ContractDetailApiResponse](#contractdetailapiresponse).

| Status | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | OK |
| `401` | Missing or invalid token |
| `403` | Token cannot access this resource |
| `404` | Contract not found |
| `429` | Rate limit exceeded |

## Schemas

### ContractApiResponse

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | integer | yes |  |
| `objectId` | integer | yes | FK to the object resource. Resolve via `getObject`. |
| `mainContractId` | integer · nullable |  | FK to the main contract when this is a sub-contract (e.g. parking, basement); null otherwise. |
| `isVacancy` | boolean | yes | True for vacancy entries (Leerstand). |
| `status` | [ContractStatus](#contractstatus) | yes |  |
| `starts` | string (date) | yes |  |
| `ends` | string (date) · nullable |  | Null = open-ended; set + not noticed = fixed-term. |
| `moveIn` | string (date) · nullable |  | Actual move-in date, if tracked. |
| `moveOut` | string (date) · nullable |  | Actual move-out date, if tracked. |
| `noticePeriodMonths` | integer | yes | Notice period in months. 0 for vacancy entries. |
| `possibleNoticeMonths` | integer[] | yes | Months (1–12) in which notice may be given. Empty for vacancy entries. |
| `firstPossibleNotice` | string (date) · nullable |  | Earliest date notice can be given; null if not set. |
| `hasVat` | boolean | yes |  |
| `qrReference` | string · nullable |  | Swiss QR-bill reference for rent payments; null if none. |
| `termination` | [ContractTerminationResponse](#contractterminationresponse) · nullable |  | Notice details; set only once notice has been given. |
| `deposit` | [ContractDepositResponse](#contractdepositresponse) · nullable |  | Security deposit; null when no deposit is recorded. |
| `persons` | [RelatedPersonResponse](#relatedpersonresponse)[] | yes | Persons linked to the contract (tenants and residents merged). |
| `currentRent` | [ContractRentResponse](#contractrentresponse) · nullable |  | The rent version effective today; null if none is effective. |

### ContractStatus

String enum, 4 values.

`upcoming`, `active`, `noticed`, `terminated`

### ContractTerminationResponse

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `noticedAt` | string (date) | yes | Date notice was given. |
| `noticedBy` | [NoticedBy](#noticedby) | yes |  |

### NoticedBy

String enum, 2 values.

`landlord`, `tenant`

### ContractDepositResponse

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | [DepositType](#deposittype) | yes |  |
| `amount` | string | yes | Deposit amount as a fixed two-decimal string. |
| `receivedAt` | string (date) · nullable |  | Date the deposit was received; null if not recorded. |
| `insuranceProvider` | string · nullable |  | Insurance provider — only set when `type` is `insurance`. |
| `insuranceNumber` | string · nullable |  | Insurance policy number — only set when `type` is `insurance`. |

### DepositType

String enum, 4 values.

`bank`, `insurance`, `zinsli`, `other`

### RelatedPersonResponse

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `personId` | integer | yes | FK to the person resource. Resolve via `getPerson`. |
| `roles` | string: `tenant` \| `owner` \| `resident`[] | yes | Roles this person holds on the entry. `tenant`/`owner` = signatory, `resident` = occupant; a person can hold both. `tenant` appears on rent contracts, `owner` on condo owners. |
| `isPrimary` | boolean | yes | True for the single primary signatory (primary `tenant`/`owner`). Always false for pure residents. |

### ContractRentResponse

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `starts` | string (date) | yes | Start of this rent version. |
| `ends` | string (date) · nullable |  | End of this rent version; null for the open-ended current version. |
| `netAmount` | string | yes | Net rent per billing cycle, as stored. Fixed two-decimal string. |
| `grossAmount` | string | yes | Gross rent per billing cycle (net + ancillary). Fixed two-decimal string. |
| `netAmountMonthly` | string | yes | Derived monthly net rent (`netAmount / billingCycle`). Fixed two-decimal string. |
| `grossAmountMonthly` | string | yes | Derived monthly gross rent (`grossAmount / billingCycle`). Fixed two-decimal string. |
| `billingCycle` | integer: `1` \| `3` \| `6` \| `12` | yes | Months per billing cycle. |
| `hasVat` | boolean | yes |  |
| `referenceInterestRate` | [ReferenceInterestRateResponse](#referenceinterestrateresponse) · nullable |  | Reference interest rate this rent is based on, or null. |
| `indexBase` | [IndexBaseResponse](#indexbaseresponse) · nullable |  | Inflation-index baseline this rent is anchored to, or null. |
| `inflationIndex` | [InflationIndexResponse](#inflationindexresponse) · nullable |  | Inflation index this rent is based on, or null. |
| `lastCostSettlement` | string · nullable |  | Last ancillary-cost settlement month, as `YYYY-MM`; null if never settled. |
| `ancillaryExpenses` | [AncillaryExpenseResponse](#ancillaryexpenseresponse)[] | yes | Agreed ancillary-expense positions for this rent version. |

### ReferenceInterestRateResponse

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `yearMonth` | string | yes | Month the rate is valid from, as `YYYY-MM`. |
| `rate` | string | yes | Reference interest rate as a percentage, decimal string (e.g. `"1.50"` means 1.50%). Sent as a string to preserve precision. |

### IndexBaseResponse

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `yearMonth` | string | yes | Baseline month, as `YYYY-MM`. |

### InflationIndexResponse

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `yearMonth` | string | yes | Month of the index figure, as `YYYY-MM`. |
| `value` | string | yes | Index figure (index points) as a decimal string. Sent as a string to preserve precision. |

### AncillaryExpenseResponse

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | yes | Position label as configured on the account. |
| `settlementMode` | [SettlementMode](#settlementmode) | yes |  |
| `amount` | string · nullable |  | Fixed amount as a two-decimal string for `flat` positions; `null` for `settled` positions (those are collected via the gross/net difference). Sent as a string to preserve precision. |

### SettlementMode

String enum, 2 values.

`flat`, `settled`

### PaginationMeta

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | integer | yes |  |
| `offset` | integer | yes |  |
| `total` | integer | yes |  |
| `hasMore` | boolean | yes |  |

### FileApiResponse

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | integer | yes | Resolve metadata via `getFile` and the binary via `downloadFile`. |
| `name` | string | yes | File name as uploaded. |
| `category` | [FileCategory](#filecategory) | yes |  |
| `mimeType` | string | yes | Stored content type. |
| `fileSize` | integer | yes | Size in bytes. |
| `uploadedAt` | string (date-time) | yes | When the file was uploaded, ISO 8601. |

### FileCategory

String enum, 18 values.

`finance`, `contracts`, `correspondence`, `protocol`, `personal_information`, `state_documents`, `repairs_and_damage`, `pictures`, `various`, `rules_and_regulations`, `locking_schedule`, `plan`, `service_contracts`, `insurance`, `offer`, `condominium_protocol`, `condominium_meeting`, `profile_image`

### ContractDetailApiResponse

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rents` | [ContractRentResponse](#contractrentresponse)[] | yes | Full rent version history, ordered by `starts`. |
| `id` | integer | yes |  |
| `objectId` | integer | yes | FK to the object resource. Resolve via `getObject`. |
| `mainContractId` | integer · nullable |  | FK to the main contract when this is a sub-contract (e.g. parking, basement); null otherwise. |
| `isVacancy` | boolean | yes | True for vacancy entries (Leerstand). |
| `status` | [ContractStatus](#contractstatus) | yes |  |
| `starts` | string (date) | yes |  |
| `ends` | string (date) · nullable |  | Null = open-ended; set + not noticed = fixed-term. |
| `moveIn` | string (date) · nullable |  | Actual move-in date, if tracked. |
| `moveOut` | string (date) · nullable |  | Actual move-out date, if tracked. |
| `noticePeriodMonths` | integer | yes | Notice period in months. 0 for vacancy entries. |
| `possibleNoticeMonths` | integer[] | yes | Months (1–12) in which notice may be given. Empty for vacancy entries. |
| `firstPossibleNotice` | string (date) · nullable |  | Earliest date notice can be given; null if not set. |
| `hasVat` | boolean | yes |  |
| `qrReference` | string · nullable |  | Swiss QR-bill reference for rent payments; null if none. |
| `termination` | [ContractTerminationResponse](#contractterminationresponse) · nullable |  | Notice details; set only once notice has been given. |
| `deposit` | [ContractDepositResponse](#contractdepositresponse) · nullable |  | Security deposit; null when no deposit is recorded. |

# Damage

| Method | Path | Operation | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/public-api/v1/{mode}/damages` | `listDamages` | List damages |
| GET | `/public-api/v1/{mode}/damages/{id}/files` | `listDamageFiles` | List files of a damage |
| GET | `/public-api/v1/{mode}/damages/{id}` | `getDamage` | Get damage details |

## GET /public-api/v1/{mode}/damages

**List damages** — `listDamages`

Returns the damages (repair tickets) reachable for the selected `{mode}`. Each
damage is anchored to a building (`buildingId`) and optionally pinned to an object
(`objectId`), an asset (`assetId`), and an assigned contractor (`serviceProviderId`).

Scope with `filter[status]`, `filter[serviceProviderId]`, `filter[objectId]`,
`filter[buildingId]`, or `filter[propertyId]`; use `q` to search across title and description.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | query | integer |  | Maximum number of items to return. limit=0 is accepted and silently treated as 1. Values above the maximum are capped to it. Default `30`. Maximum `100`. |
| `offset` | query | integer |  | Number of items to skip. Use with limit for pagination. Default `0`. |
| `q` | query | string |  | Free-text search across: title, description. Case-insensitive partial match; every word must match one of these fields (so "Peter Berger" matches first and last name in separate fields). Combine with filter[...] keys to narrow further. |
| `filter[status]` | query | string: `new` \| `offer_requested` \| `order_placed` \| `invoice_pending` \| `correction_needed` \| `finished` |  | Restricts results to records matching the given status. |
| `filter[serviceProviderId]` | query | integer |  | Restricts results to records belonging to the given serviceProvider id. |
| `filter[objectId]` | query | integer |  | Restricts results to records belonging to the given object id. |
| `filter[buildingId]` | query | integer |  | Restricts results to records belonging to the given building id. |
| `filter[propertyId]` | query | integer |  | Restricts results to records belonging to the given property id. |
| `sort` | query | string: `id` \| `-id` \| `dateOfDamage` \| `-dateOfDamage` |  | Sort field. Prefix with `-` for descending order (e.g. `-id`). Allowed: id, dateOfDamage. |
| `mode` | path | string: `rent` \| `condo` | yes | Business domain for the request. Use `rent` for rental-management data, `condo` for condominium-ownership data. The selected mode constrains every related resource. |

**List capabilities**

- **Searchable (`q`):** title, description
- **Filterable:** `filter[status]` (`new`, `offer_requested`, `order_placed`, `invoice_pending`, `correction_needed`, `finished`), `filter[serviceProviderId]`, `filter[objectId]`, `filter[buildingId]`, `filter[propertyId]`
- **Sortable:** `id`, `dateOfDamage` (prefix `-` for descending)
- **Page size:** default `30`, maximum `100`

**Response** — `200` returns a list envelope around [DamageApiResponse](#damageapiresponse).

| Status | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | OK |
| `400` | Invalid query parameters |
| `401` | Missing or invalid token |
| `403` | Token cannot access this resource |
| `429` | Rate limit exceeded |

**Example response**

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": 1,
      "buildingId": 12,
      "propertyId": 7,
      "objectId": 789,
      "assetId": 4021,
      "serviceProviderId": 55,
      "status": "new",
      "title": "Geschirrspüler undicht",
      "description": "string",
      "cause": "string",
      "dateOfDamage": "2026-05-28",
      "estimatedCost": "350.00"
    }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "pagination": {
      "limit": 30,
      "offset": 0,
      "total": 1,
      "hasMore": false
    }
  }
}
```

One of: `finance`, `contracts`, `correspondence`, `protocol`, `personal_information`, `state_documents`, `repairs_and_damage`, `pictures`, `various`, `rules_and_regulations`, `locking_schedule`, `plan`, `service_contracts`, `insurance`, `offer`, `condominium_protocol`, `condominium_meeting`, `profile_image`. |
| `sort` | query | string: `id` \| `-id` \| `name` \| `-name` \| `uploadedAt` \| `-uploadedAt` \| `fileSize` \| `-fileSize` |  | Sort field. Prefix with `-` for descending order (e.g. `-id`). Allowed: id, name, uploadedAt, fileSize. |
| `id` | path | integer | yes |  |
| `mode` | path | string: `rent` \| `condo` | yes | Business domain for the request. Use `rent` for rental-management data, `condo` for condominium-ownership data. The selected mode constrains every related resource. |

- **Filterable:** `filter[category]` (`finance`, `contracts`, `correspondence`, `protocol`, `personal_information`, `state_documents`, `repairs_and_damage`, `pictures`, `various`, `rules_and_regulations`, `locking_schedule`, `plan`, `service_contracts`, `insurance`, `offer`, `condominium_protocol`, `condominium_meeting`, `profile_image`)
- **Sortable:** `id`, `name`, `uploadedAt`, `fileSize` (prefix `-` for descending)

| Status | Description |

```json
  "data": [
    {
      "id": 4711,

      "category": "finance",
      "mimeType": "application/pdf",
      "fileSize": 184320,
      "uploadedAt": "2026-03-14T09:12:00+01:00"
    }
```

## GET /public-api/v1/{mode}/damages/{id}

**Get damage details** — `getDamage`

Returns a single damage by id, including its status, title, description, cause,
date, and estimated cost, plus the building/object/asset/service-provider it relates to.

Use `listDamages` for discovery when the id is unknown.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | integer | yes |  |
| `mode` | path | string: `rent` \| `condo` | yes | Business domain for the request. Use `rent` for rental-management data, `condo` for condominium-ownership data. The selected mode constrains every related resource. |

**Response** — `200` returns [DamageApiResponse](#damageapiresponse).

| Status | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | OK |
| `401` | Missing or invalid token |
| `403` | Token cannot access this resource |
| `404` | Damage not found |
| `429` | Rate limit exceeded |

**Example response**

```json
{
  "id": 1,
  "buildingId": 12,
  "propertyId": 7,
  "objectId": 789,
  "assetId": 4021,
  "serviceProviderId": 55,
  "status": "new",
  "title": "Geschirrspüler undicht",
  "description": "string",
  "cause": "string",
  "dateOfDamage": "2026-05-28",
  "estimatedCost": "350.00"
}
```

# DebitorInvoice

| Method | Path | Operation | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/public-api/v1/{mode}/debitor-invoices` | `listDebitorInvoices` | List debitor invoices |
| GET | `/public-api/v1/{mode}/debitor-invoices/{id}` | `getDebitorInvoice` | Get debitor invoice details |

## GET /public-api/v1/{mode}/debitor-invoices

**List debitor invoices** — `listDebitorInvoices`

Returns the debitor invoices (receivables issued to tenants/owners) reachable for
the selected `{mode}`, across all sources (rent, ancillary-expense settlements,
final accounts, manual invoices). Draft and vacancy invoices are never returned.
Each row carries the derived `status`, `isOverdue`, the aggregated `paidAmount` /
`openAmount` balance, and the linked recipient `persons`; the inline `positions`
and `payments` are on the detail endpoint.

Narrow with `filter[status]`, `filter[isOverdue]` (the dunning filter),
`filter[type]`, `filter[personId]` (the tenant-portal balance filter),
`filter[contractId]`, `filter[objectId]`, `filter[propertyId]`,
`filter[mandateId]`, or the `filter[dueDateFrom]` / `filter[dueDateTo]` range.
Use `q` to search by invoice number or label.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | query | integer |  | Maximum number of items to return. limit=0 is accepted and silently treated as 1. Values above the maximum are capped to it. Default `30`. Maximum `100`. |
| `offset` | query | integer |  | Number of items to skip. Use with limit for pagination. Default `0`. |
| `q` | query | string |  | Free-text search across: reference, label. Case-insensitive partial match; every word must match one of these fields (so "Peter Berger" matches first and last name in separate fields). Combine with filter[...] keys to narrow further. |
| `filter[status]` | query | string: `sent` \| `partially_paid` \| `paid` \| `overpaid` |  | Restricts results to records matching the given status. |
| `filter[isOverdue]` | query | string: `true` \| `false` |  | Restricts results to records matching the given isOverdue. |
| `filter[type]` | query | string: `rent` \| `ancillary_expense` \| `final_account` \| `manual` \| `budget` |  | Restricts results to records matching the given type. |
| `filter[personId]` | query | integer |  | Restricts results to records belonging to the given person id. |
| `filter[contractId]` | query | integer |  | Restricts results to records belonging to the given contract id. |
| `filter[objectId]` | query | integer |  | Restricts results to records belonging to the given object id. |
| `filter[propertyId]` | query | integer |  | Restricts results to records belonging to the given property id. |
| `filter[mandateId]` | query | integer |  | Restricts results to records belonging to the given mandate id. |
| `filter[dueDateFrom]` | query | string (date) |  | Lower (inclusive) bound: only records whose dueDate is on or after this value. |
| `filter[dueDateTo]` | query | string (date) |  | Upper (inclusive) bound: only records whose dueDate is on or before this value. |
| `sort` | query | string: `id` \| `-id` \| `invoiceDate` \| `-invoiceDate` \| `dueDate` \| `-dueDate` |  | Sort field. Prefix with `-` for descending order (e.g. `-id`). Allowed: id, invoiceDate, dueDate. |
| `mode` | path | string: `rent` \| `condo` | yes | Business domain for the request. Use `rent` for rental-management data, `condo` for condominium-ownership data. The selected mode constrains every related resource. |

**List capabilities**

- **Searchable (`q`):** reference, label
- **Filterable:** `filter[status]` (`sent`, `partially_paid`, `paid`, `overpaid`), `filter[isOverdue]` (`true`, `false`), `filter[type]` (`rent`, `ancillary_expense`, `final_account`, `manual`, `budget`), `filter[personId]`, `filter[contractId]`, `filter[objectId]`, `filter[propertyId]`, `filter[mandateId]`, `filter[dueDateFrom]`, `filter[dueDateTo]`
- **Sortable:** `id`, `invoiceDate`, `dueDate` (prefix `-` for descending)
- **Page size:** default `30`, maximum `100`

**Response** — `200` returns a list envelope around [DebitorInvoiceApiResponse](#debitorinvoiceapiresponse).

| Status | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | OK |
| `400` | Invalid query parameters |
| `401` | Missing or invalid token |
| `403` | Token cannot access this resource |
| `429` | Rate limit exceeded |

**Example response**

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": 1,
      "contractId": 456,
      "objectId": 789,
      "propertyId": 7,
      "reference": "100001234",
      "label": "Mietzins Juni 2026",
      "type": "rent",
      "status": "sent",
      "isOverdue": true,
      "invoiceDate": "2026-05-20",
      "dueDate": "2026-06-01",
      "periodFrom": "2025-01-31",
      "periodTo": "2025-01-31",
      "currency": "CHF",
      "amount": "1700.00",
      "paidAmount": "1000.00",
      "openAmount": "700.00",
      "qrReference": "string",
      "reminderLevel": 1,
      "lastReminderAt": "2025-01-31",
      "persons": [
        {
          "personId": 123,
          "isPrimary": true
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "pagination": {
      "limit": 30,
      "offset": 0,
      "total": 1,
      "hasMore": false
    }
  }
}
```

## GET /public-api/v1/{mode}/debitor-invoices/{id}

**Get debitor invoice details** — `getDebitorInvoice`

Returns a single debitor invoice by id, including the recipient `persons`, the
inline `positions` and matched `payments`, and the derived `status` / `isOverdue`
and `paidAmount` / `openAmount` balance. Returns 404 when the invoice does not
exist, is a draft or vacancy invoice, is outside the token's scope, or does not
belong to the selected `{mode}`.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | integer | yes |  |
| `mode` | path | string: `rent` \| `condo` | yes | Business domain for the request. Use `rent` for rental-management data, `condo` for condominium-ownership data. The selected mode constrains every related resource. |

**Response** — `200` returns [DebitorInvoiceDetailApiResponse](#debitorinvoicedetailapiresponse).

| Status | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | OK |
| `401` | Missing or invalid token |
| `403` | Token cannot access this resource |
| `404` | Debitor invoice not found |
| `429` | Rate limit exceeded |

**Example response**

```json
{
  "positions": [
    {
      "label": "Nettomiete",
      "type": "normal",
      "amount": "1500.00"
    }
  ],
  "payments": [
    {
      "paidAt": "2026-06-05",
      "amount": "1000.00"
    }
  ],
  "id": 1,
  "contractId": 456,
  "objectId": 789,
  "propertyId": 7,
  "reference": "100001234",
  "label": "Mietzins Juni 2026",
  "type": "rent",
  "status": "sent",
  "isOverdue": true,
  "invoiceDate": "2026-05-20",
  "dueDate": "2026-06-01",
  "periodFrom": "2025-01-31",
  "periodTo": "2025-01-31",
  "currency": "CHF",
  "amount": "1700.00",
  "paidAmount": "1000.00",
  "openAmount": "700.00",
  "qrReference": "string",
  "reminderLevel": 1,
  "lastReminderAt": "2025-01-31",
  "persons": [
    {
      "personId": 123,
      "isPrimary": true
    }
  ]
}
```

# File

| Method | Path | Operation | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/public-api/v1/files/{id}/content` | `downloadFile` | Download a file |
| GET | `/public-api/v1/files/{id}` | `getFile` | Get file metadata |

## GET /public-api/v1/files/{id}/content

**Download a file** — `downloadFile`

Streams the file's bytes as an attachment, named as it was uploaded. Visibility is
identical to `getFile`. Counts against the ordinary request rate limit.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | integer | yes |  |

| Status | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | The file, as an attachment. |
| `401` | Missing or invalid token |
| `403` | Token cannot access this resource |
| `404` | File not found |
| `429` | Rate limit exceeded |

## GET /public-api/v1/files/{id}

**Get file metadata** — `getFile`

Returns a file's metadata and the attachments of it you may see. There is no top-level
`category`: the category belongs to the attachment, and one file can be attached to
several owners with a different category on each.

A file whose only owners are outside your scope, or of a kind this API does not expose,
is indistinguishable from one that does not exist. Use `downloadFile` for the binary.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | integer | yes |  |

**Response** — `200` returns [FileDetailApiResponse](#filedetailapiresponse).

| Status | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | OK |
| `401` | Missing or invalid token |
| `403` | Token cannot access this resource |
| `404` | File not found |
| `429` | Rate limit exceeded |

**Example response**

```json
{
  "id": 1,
  "name": "Hausordnung.pdf",
  "mimeType": "application/pdf",
  "fileSize": 184320,
  "uploadedAt": "2026-03-14T09:12:00+01:00",
  "owners": [
    {
      "type": "property",
      "id": 12,
      "category": "finance"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Schemas

### FileDetailApiResponse

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | integer | yes |  |
| `name` | string | yes | File name as uploaded. |
| `mimeType` | string | yes | Stored content type. |
| `fileSize` | integer | yes | Size in bytes. |
| `uploadedAt` | string (date-time) | yes | When the file was uploaded, ISO 8601. |
| `owners` | [FileOwnerResponse](#fileownerresponse)[] | yes | The visible attachments of this file. Never empty — a file with no visible owner returns 404. There is no top-level `category`: it belongs to the attachment, and one file can be attached to several owners with a different category on each. |

### FileOwnerResponse

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | [FileOwnerType](#fileownertype) | yes |  |
| `id` | integer | yes | Id of that object, resolvable on its own resource. |
| `category` | [FileCategory](#filecategory) | yes |  |

### FileOwnerType

String enum, 9 values.

`property`, `building`, `object`, `damage`, `contract`, `owner`, `person`, `mandate`, `user`

### FileCategory

String enum, 18 values.

`finance`, `contracts`, `correspondence`, `protocol`, `personal_information`, `state_documents`, `repairs_and_damage`, `pictures`, `various`, `rules_and_regulations`, `locking_schedule`, `plan`, `service_contracts`, `insurance`, `offer`, `condominium_protocol`, `condominium_meeting`, `profile_image`

# FiscalYear

| Method | Path | Operation | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| GET | `/public-api/v1/{mode}/fiscal-years/{id}` | `getFiscalYear` | Get a fiscal year |

## GET /public-api/v1/{mode}/fiscal-years

**List fiscal years** — `listFiscalYears`

Returns the fiscal years reachable for the selected `{mode}`: regular accounting
years (per property) and consolidation years (per mandate). Internal
ancillary-expense and reporting periods are never returned.

Narrow with `filter[propertyId]` (accounting years), `filter[mandateId]`
(consolidation years), `filter[type]`, or `filter[isLocked]`.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | query | integer |  | Maximum number of items to return. limit=0 is accepted and silently treated as 1. Values above the maximum are capped to it. Default `30`. Maximum `100`. |
| `offset` | query | integer |  | Number of items to skip. Use with limit for pagination. Default `0`. |
| `q` | query | string |  | Free-text search. Case-insensitive partial match; every word must match one of the searchable fields. Combine with filter[...] keys to narrow further. |
| `filter[propertyId]` | query | integer |  | Restricts results to records belonging to the given property id. |
| `filter[mandateId]` | query | integer |  | Restricts results to records belonging to the given mandate id. |
| `filter[type]` | query | string: `accounting` \| `consolidation` |  | Restricts results to records matching the given type. |
| `filter[isLocked]` | query | string: `true` \| `false` |  | Restricts results to records matching the given isLocked. |
| `sort` | query | string: `starts` \| `-starts` \| `id` \| `-id` |  | Sort field. Prefix with `-` for descending order (e.g. `-starts`). Allowed: starts, id. |
| `mode` | path | string: `rent` \| `condo` | yes | Business domain for the request. Use `rent` for rental-management data, `condo` for condominium-ownership data. The selected mode constrains every related resource. |

**List capabilities**

- **Searchable (`q`):** Free-text search
- **Filterable:** `filter[propertyId]`, `filter[mandateId]`, `filter[type]` (`accounting`, `consolidation`), `filter[isLocked]` (`true`, `false`)
- **Sortable:** `starts`, `id` (prefix `-` for descending)
- **Page size:** default `30`, maximum `100`

**Response** — `200` returns a list envelope around [FiscalYearApiResponse](#fiscalyearapiresponse).

| Status | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | OK |
| `400` | Invalid query parameters |
| `401` | Missing or invalid token |
| `403` | Token cannot access this resource |
| `429` | Rate limit exceeded |

**Example response**

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": 1,
      "propertyId": 7,
      "mandateId": null,
      "label": "2025",
      "type": "accounting",
      "starts": "2025-01-01",
      "ends": "2025-12-31",
      "isLocked": true
    }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "pagination": {
      "limit": 30,
      "offset": 0,
      "total": 1,
      "hasMore": false
    }
  }
}
```

## GET /public-api/v1/mandates

**List mandates** — `listMandates`

Returns mandates the calling token can reach.

A mandate is the top of the Public API resource hierarchy: `Mandate → Property → Building → Object`. Every other resource lives under exactly one mandate, so this endpoint is the discovery starting point.

No filter keys are exposed (mandates are not scoped by any other resource); use `q` for free-text search across the mandate name, second name, street, postal code and city. Read `type` on each returned mandate (`rent` or `condo`) to decide which `{mode}` to pass on related endpoints.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | query | integer |  | Maximum number of items to return. limit=0 is accepted and silently treated as 1. Values above the maximum are capped to it. Default `30`. Maximum `100`. |
| `offset` | query | integer |  | Number of items to skip. Use with limit for pagination. Default `0`. |
| `q` | query | string |  | Free-text search across: name1, name2, street, postcode, city. Case-insensitive partial match; every word must match one of these fields (so "Peter Berger" matches first and last name in separate fields). Combine with filter[...] keys to narrow further. |
| `sort` | query | string: `id` \| `-id` \| `name` \| `-name` |  | Sort field. Prefix with `-` for descending order (e.g. `-id`). Allowed: id, name. |

**List capabilities**

- **Searchable (`q`):** name1, name2, street, postcode, city
- **Sortable:** `id`, `name` (prefix `-` for descending)
- **Page size:** default `30`, maximum `100`

**Response** — `200` returns a list envelope around [MandateApiResponse](#mandateapiresponse).

| Status | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | OK |
| `400` | Invalid query parameters |
| `401` | Missing or invalid token |
| `403` | Token cannot access this resource |
| `429` | Rate limit exceeded |

**Example response**

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": 1,
      "name1": "Müller",
      "name2": "Anna",
      "contactType": "natural",
      "type": "rent",
      "salutation": "unspecified",
      "email": "string",
      "phone": "string",
      "website": "string",
      "address": {
        "street": "string",
        "houseNumber": "string",
        "postcode": "string",
        "city": "string",
        "country": "string"
      }
    }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "pagination": {
      "limit": 30,
      "offset": 0,
      "total": 1,
      "hasMore": false
    }
  }
}
```

| `q` | query | string |  | Free-text search across: name. Case-insensitive partial match; every word must match one of these fields (so "Peter Berger" matches first and last name in separate fields). Combine with filter[...] keys to narrow further. |

One of: `finance`, `contracts`, `correspondence`, `protocol`, `personal_information`, `state_documents`, `repairs_and_damage`, `pictures`, `various`, `rules_and_regulations`, `locking_schedule`, `plan`, `service_contracts`, `insurance`, `offer`, `condominium_protocol`, `condominium_meeting`, `profile_image`. |

- **Sortable:** `id`, `name`, `uploadedAt`, `fileSize` (prefix `-` for descending)
- **Page size:** default `30`, maximum `100`

**Response** — `200` returns a list envelope around [FileApiResponse](#fileapiresponse).

## GET /public-api/v1/mandates/{id}

**Get mandate details** — `getMandate`

Returns a single mandate by id, including its contact, address, and `type` (`rent` or `condo`).

Use `listMandates` for discovery when the id is unknown. The returned `type` determines which `{mode}` to pass on related endpoints (`getProperty`, `getBuilding`, `getObject`, and their list counterparts).

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | integer | yes |  |

**Response** — `200` returns [MandateApiResponse](#mandateapiresponse).

| Status | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | OK |
| `401` | Missing or invalid token |
| `403` | Token cannot access this resource |
| `404` | Mandate not found |
| `429` | Rate limit exceeded |

**Example response**

```json
{
  "id": 1,
  "name1": "Müller",
  "name2": "Anna",
  "contactType": "natural",
  "type": "rent",
  "salutation": "unspecified",
  "email": "string",
  "phone": "string",
  "website": "string",
  "address": {
    "street": "string",
    "houseNumber": "string",
    "postcode": "string",
    "city": "string",
    "country": "string"
  }
}
```

# Object

| Method | Path | Operation | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| GET | `/public-api/v1/{mode}/objects/{id}/files` | `listObjectFiles` | List files of an object |
